i.norm:
Verifies that a node can be removed during iteration via {@link Node#remove()}.

Key behaviour under test: calling {@code node.remove()} inside the iteration loop removes the node from the document tree. The removed node itself still appears in the "seen" log (because {@code next()} already returned it), but its descendants are skipped — the iterator detects the structural change and jumps past the removed subtree.
Arrange: a document with two outer divs; the first outer div contains two inner divs, each holding two paragraphs.
--- First pass: remove div#1 mid-iteration --- Act
Assert: div#1 appears in "seen" (it was already returned before removal), but its children (p;One;p;Two) are absent because the iterator skipped them after the structural change.
The document itself no longer contains div#1 or its descendants.
--- Second pass: remove div#2 mid-iteration --- Act
Assert: same pattern — div#2 appears in "seen" but its children (p;Three;p;Four) are skipped.
The document now contains neither div#1 nor div#2.
